solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Soldiers may engage them at the crack of dawn

definitions.text: Soldiers may engage them at the crack of dawn

parts.words: Soldiers may engage them at the crack of dawn
parts.note: soldiers are strips of buttered toast dipped into a runny-yolked breakfast egg, which is opened (cracked) early in the morning

explanation.surface: Troops go into battle with an enemy at first light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soldiers' are not troops: in Britain they are fingers of toast for dipping into a boiled egg, and 'crack of dawn' is both daybreak and the cracking of the shell at breakfast.
explanation.definitionFit: Breakfast eggs with runny yolks are what toast fingers are dunked into, and they are eaten early in the day.

clue.text: Discharge rifle

definitions.meaning: to dismiss someone from a job
to plunder or ransack, as an army pillages a town

explanation.surface: A soldier fires his gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rifle' looks like the gun being fired, but here it is the verb meaning to ransack.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are verbs: firing an employee, and looting a captured town.

clue.text: Number four in empty fridge

indicators.note: in means the numeral sits inside the remaining letters
an empty fridge keeps only its shell, so just the first and last letters of the word stay

parts.note: IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A tally of four items left in an otherwise bare fridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'four' looks like part of the count of items, but it is the Roman numeral, and 'empty' strips the fridge to its outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A cardinal numeral, one more than four, is a number.

clue.text: Healing ointment revitalised foliaged tree

parts.note: a balm is a soothing healing salve

indicators.note: revitalised suggests the letters of foliaged are given new life in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A soothing salve has brought a leafy tree back to health.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revitalised' rearranges FOLIAGED into OF GILEAD. 'Healing ointment' looks like the definition, but the answer is defined by 'tree'.
explanation.definitionFit: This phrase names a small Middle Eastern evergreen yielding aromatic resin, and also some poplars and firs.

clue.text: Newton is a Chartered Accountant up in Scotland

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: CA is the abbreviation for a chartered accountant, the usual title in Scotland

explanation.surface: A man called Newton turns out to be a Scottish accountant.
explanation.walkthrough: In Scotland a qualified accountant is styled a Chartered Accountant; 'up' reverses the abbreviation, as this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Isaac Newton, the physicist, bore this first name, so the surname clues the forename.

clue.text: Café advertisement left out derv spillage

indicators.note: left out means some letters of the long word are missing from the final word
spillage suggests the remaining letters are scattered into a new order

parts.note: derv is British diesel fuel for road vehicles; here its letters are the ones dropped

explanation.surface: A café's poster is ruined by diesel spilled across it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left out' removes D, E, R, V from ADVERTISEMENT, and 'spillage' shuffles what remains (ATISEMENT). Derv is British diesel fuel.
explanation.definitionFit: This French borrowing names a small bar or café selling drink, a word familiar from the First World War.

clue.text: See 1 across
Scribe spiritually?

parts.note: to write as a phantom would, i.e. compose text that appears under someone else's name

explanation.surface: Writing guided by a spirit, as at a séance.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the pun: a spirit is a ghost, and a ghost in publishing writes for someone else.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing books or speeches credited to another person is done unseen, like a phantom.

clue.text: Meddler left special lubricants at the front

indicators.note: at the front puts the special lubricants before the word for left

parts.note: oils are lubricants
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: A busybody abandoned special lubricants near the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at the front' places SP OILS ahead of PORT, the nautical left side.
explanation.definitionFit: A killjoy who interferes and ruins others' fun is a kind of meddler.

clue.text: A cat Calvin butchered in Rio neighbourhood

indicators.note: butchered suggests the words are hacked up and their letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A cat owned by Calvin was killed somewhere in Rio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butchered' rearranges the letters of A CAT CALVIN.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a district in the north zone of Rio de Janeiro, Brazil.

clue.text: Repeatedly calling for attention to toy

indicators.note: repeatedly means the call is given twice in a row

parts.note: yo is a shout to get someone's attention

explanation.surface: Someone keeps calling out for notice to a plaything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Repeatedly' doubles YO, the shout for attention.
explanation.definitionFit: A spool on a string that spins down and climbs back up is a classic plaything.

clue.text: Encounter hardship, so criticise a poor temporary solution from Microsoft, perhaps

parts.note: to hit out at is to criticise
poor means bad
a patch is a software fix, as Microsoft issues for Windows

explanation.surface: Having a rough time, so attacking a shoddy quick fix from a software giant.
explanation.definitionFit: To go through a difficult spell is an idiom for meeting hardship.

clue.text: Cautious Milton to con man "No, no criminal"

indicators.note: no means without, so the letters of the quoted word are taken away
criminal suggests the remaining letters are twisted into a crooked new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Milton tells a swindler he is no crook.
explanation.walkthrough: From MILTON TO CON MAN take N and O (the 'No' with 'no' meaning without), and 'criminal' shuffles the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone guarded who will not commit to a view is cautious.

clue.text: Hoax cover admitted by press chief, sheepish & sorry

parts.note: a sham is a hoax

indicators.note: admitted by means the cover word is let in between the editor's letters

parts.note: ED is short for editor, the chief of a newspaper
to face a wall is to cover it with a surface layer

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor owns up to a cover-up and looks embarrassed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cover' is a verb here, as in facing a wall with stone; 'admitted by' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Looking ashamed and embarrassed is a fair synonym for sheepish and sorry.

clue.text: Promise air conditioning for showman

indicators.note: conditioning suggests the words are worked on and reshaped into another form

explanation.surface: A pledge to install air conditioning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conditioning' rearranges PROMISE AIR; 'air conditioning' reads as one phrase but splits.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatrical promoter or manager who stages productions is a showman.

clue.text: Native in formal dress embracing king

parts.note: being in means being at home

indicators.note: embracing means the dress wraps around the king's letter

parts.note: a gown is formal dress
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A local person in evening wear hugging the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link word but means being at home; R is rex, Latin for king, and 'embracing' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Produce raised locally rather than imported is native to the place.

clue.text: No more blueprint outstanding with the bank

definitions.note: a phrase standing for the noun, a debt owed to the bank

parts.note: over means finished, no more
a draft is a plan or blueprint

explanation.surface: A plan is finished and is still waiting at the bank.
explanation.definitionFit: Money drawn beyond what is in the account is a sum owed to the bank.

clue.text: See 22
Right for all to see replacement for round wall painting

indicators.note: replacement for means one letter is swapped in where another stood

parts.note: moral means right, ethical
O is round in shape
U is the British film certificate for a universal audience, fit for all to see

explanation.surface: An ethical stance on public display replaced the circular wall art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replacement for' swaps the O (round) in MORAL for U, the British film rating meaning suitable for everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: A large picture painted directly onto a wall is the standard sense.

clue.text: Old farm vehicle & exhaust fan

parts.note: ex means former or old
a tractor is a farm vehicle

explanation.surface: A veteran farm machine and a ventilator side by side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exhaust fan' looks like two separate items, but it is one definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A fan that draws out stale air or fumes is a device for removing them.

clue.text: Almost fine dish chaps fried for traditional food

indicators.note: fried suggests the letters are cooked up into a new arrangement
almost means the last letter of the word is cut off

explanation.surface: Fellows nearly cooked a good dish in the fryer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' trims FINE to FIN; 'fried' shuffles FIN with DISH CHAPS.
explanation.definitionFit: Battered fried cod with chunky potato pieces is the classic British takeaway meal.

clue.text: Rubbishy enactment restricts wild animal

indicators.note: restricts means the phrase holds the answer within its letters

explanation.surface: A poorly drafted law limits a beast's freedom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'restricts' points to the letters spanning rubbisHY ENActment.
explanation.definitionFit: A scavenging African carnivore known for its laugh-like call is a wild animal.

clue.text: Cast Mike with a part in "Travel"

indicators.note: cast suggests the letters are thrown into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An actor named Mike is cast in a stage show called Travel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' rearranges MIKE with A PART; theatrical 'cast' and 'part' are the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: To go on a journey is to travel.

clue.text: Peel with gusto

definitions.meaning: the thin outer skin of a citrus fruit

explanation.surface: Stripping fruit enthusiastically.
explanation.definitionFit: Citrus rind and keen enjoyment share this one word.

clue.text: Brusque scoundrel with model

parts.note: a cur is a contemptible scoundrel
the Model T was Ford's early car, so T can stand for model

explanation.surface: A rude rascal accompanying a fashion model.
explanation.walkthrough: T stands for the Ford Model T.
explanation.definitionFit: Short and abrupt in manner is a synonym for brusque.

clue.text: Own a timed device for an easy life

definitions.note: a noun phrase standing for the verb phrase meaning to enjoy such comfort

parts.note: to own is to have

indicators.note: device, as in something devised, suggests the letters are reworked into a new form

explanation.surface: Buying a timer gadget to make life simple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'device' rearranges A TIMED after HAVE for 'Own'.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to be assured of success and comfort, i.e. to enjoy a cushy existence.

clue.text: Give up deposit

definitions.meaning: to set down or leave something somewhere

explanation.surface: Abandoning a payment.
explanation.definitionFit: Quitting a habit and setting a package down are both expressed by this verb.

clue.text: A loving feeling for that net cam development

indicators.note: development, as in a film being developed, suggests the letters are processed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Fond feelings for a newly developed internet camera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'development' rearranges THAT NET CAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Affection or fondness for someone is a loving feeling.
